content: In quite some cases simp_all? only is not automatically replaceable with simp only. One these would be if simp_all uses a local hypothesis. Even though this is in some sense restricted to implicitness and hidden side effects only within the local context I tend to still always replace the suggested simp_all with simp so that I have explicit and easy to trace effects of what is used where (and faster as a bonus). Would it not be possible to enhance the simp_all? hints with automatic replacement using simp where used local hypothesis are also included in the hint like simp only [some_local_hypothesis_that_was_used]?

simp_all genuinely uses a different approach than simp, so it's certainly not always possible to give a simp only suggestion that would work.

Some concrete examples would be helpful.

simp_all genuinely uses a different approach than simp, so it's certainly not always possible to give a simp only suggestion that would work.

Ok, fair enough point so let's assume that in some cases simp_all may remain irreducible to simp. This doesn't mean that there can be no more useful cases where it would still be reducible to simp.

Some concrete examples would be helpful.

Here is a simple illustration:

theorem a (h : b = 2) : b = 2 := by
  simp_all? only

displays

Try this:
  [apply] simp_all only

while the following is more explicit

theorem a (h : b = 2) : b = 2 := by
  simp only [h]

and I would be happy if the suggested output by simp_all? instead is

Try this:
  [apply] simp only [h]
